newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG RECOVER EUROPEAN FORM TO CRUSH LIVERPOOL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG RECOVER EUROPEAN FORM TO CRUSH LIVERPOOL.

text.p: Paris St Germain took a giant step towards their second consecutive European Cup Winners' Cup final when they crushed Liverpool 3-0 in their semifinal first leg at the Parc des Princes on Thursday.

The Parisians, bidding to become the first team to retain the trophy, took an early lead through Brazilian Leonardo, who took advantage of a clumsy save from Liverpool goalkeeper David James to open the scoring in the 10th minute.
James was again to blame for PSG's second goal as he failed to catch a cross from Jerome Leroy and allowed midfielder Benoit Cauet to make the score 2-0 just three minute before the break.
But there was nothing James could do to stop PSG's third goal, scored from close range by Leroy in the 83rd minute from a pass by substitute Cyrille Pouget.
"David has had a very difficult season but to be fair with him I must say that the defence was not very good tonight," Liverpool manager Roy Evans admitted.

Parisian coach Ricardo drew a comparison with his team's disappointing league performances, saying: "We're a different team in European cups, don't ask me why, but we must keep our feet on the ground and remember there is a second leg."
Liverpool were defensively naive against the experienced Parisians, playing in their fifth consecutive European semifinal.
Leonardo was especially impressive and started many of PSG's most dangerous moves, scoring the first goal and setting up Cauet for the second.
His first goal, so early in the match, was the catalyst for the Parisians' commanding victory.
"The first goal was a huge relief and we were very relaxed afterwards," said goalkeeper Bernard Lama, who was in much better form than his Liverpool counterpart.
"But they were tough opposition in the second half and the third goal was crucial because they will be hard to beat at Anfield."
History shows Liverpool have always lost away to French teams in European cup competitions before qualifying at Anfield in the second leg.
But they will need an outstanding performance in two weeks to retain their hopes of lifting the only European trophy they have yet to win.

"Nothing functioned tonight. We did not play as a team. We played slowly with individual minds," Evans said. "I'm not surprised by PSG's performance because they have talent. We lacked patience. We lacked pride."
